questions.question: Which of these tire conditions is NOT a problem?

options.text: Rear tires with at least 2/32 inch of tread

questions.correctAnswerText: Rear tires with at least 2/32 inch of tread
questions.explanation: Check that air pressure is correct. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Rear tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread. Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires.

questions.question: If there is a vehicle inspection report, what should you do?

options.text: Inspect the vehicle first, then compare your notes with the report.
Read the report first when you start your inspection.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the report first when you start your inspection.
questions.explanation: Always review any inspection report from the previous driver as your first step.

questions.question: What affects how far it takes to stop?
questions.explanation: Your stopping distance depends on your speed, your vehicle's weight, and how slippery the road is.

questions.question: If you don't know the area where you need to back up, what should you do?

options.text: Get out and walk around to see the area first.
Don't use both side mirrors because it's distracting.
Wait for someone else to back up so you can watch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around to see the area first.
questions.explanation: Get out and check your path before backing up. Look for anything that could hit your sides or the top of your vehicle.

questions.question: Is a curve's posted design speed safe for buses?

options.text: Safe for all vehicles including buses
The minimum speed for the curve

questions.explanation: A bus can roll over or slide off the road even at the posted speed for a curve. Always drive slower on curves in a bus.

questions.question: What condition should the exhaust system be in?
questions.explanation: The exhaust system must have no loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to reduce crashes when turning right?

options.text: Keep the rear close to the curb
Leave open space on your right side

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave open space on your right side
questions.explanation: When turning right, keep your rear close to the curb. Leaving space on the right may make other drivers think you're turning left, so they might pass on your right.

questions.question: Can you use tires of different sizes?
questions.explanation: Tires must all be the same size. If you find mismatched tires during an inspection, they must be replaced.

questions.question: What tread depth is needed on non-front tires of a commercial vehicle?
questions.explanation: Front tires need 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need 2/32 inch of tread.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature is too high, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and check for problems

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check for problems
questions.explanation: Stop driving right away if the coolant temperature is too high. Something could be wrong that could cause engine failure or fire.

questions.question: What is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive slowly and carefully near road workers.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not use the brakes. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: If you meet an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, stay out of their way if you can. Do not make eye contact, as this may anger them more. Ignore any hand gestures they make.

questions.question: When checking your tires, you should avoid finding:

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems must not be cut or cracked. All tire sizes must match.

questions.question: Which of these is not acceptable emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three liquid burning flares, and a working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you can check all of these except:
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, you will check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt if the vehicle has them.

questions.question: If brakes get too hot going downhill, they may:
questions.explanation: Using brakes too much can make them overheat and stop working well. This is called "brake fade."

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, a bus driver should:

options.text: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest track.
Drive carefully but only stop if a train is coming.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest track.
questions.explanation: A bus driver must stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks and check for trains. The driver may open the door to see or hear any approaching trains better.

questions.question: At railroad crossings, bus drivers:

options.text: Do not need to stop but must slow down 25 mph below the speed limit.
Do not need to stop but must open the door to listen for trains.
Must stop and check for trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and check for trains.
questions.explanation: When driving a bus at a railroad crossing, you must stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track and look and listen for trains. Only cross when you are sure no trains are coming. You do not need to stop at streetcar crossings, when a police officer is directing traffic, at green traffic signals, or at crossings marked "exempt" or "abandoned."
